title: The Lord who loves you back, and loves you first
subtitle: The Most Loving, who loves His servants and is loved by them
intro: Al-Wadud (الْوَدُودُ) means the Most Loving, the One who loves His servants who turn to Him, shows that love through His gifts and forgiveness, and is Himself the One most worthy of being loved. It tells you that your relationship with Allah can be one of love, not only of rules.

root.sense: Wudd is warm, open affection: love that wants closeness and shows itself. The Quran uses it for the affection placed between spouses (30:21). Scholars explain Wadud as both the One who loves intensely and the One who is loved; the name carries both directions at once.

row.title: He loves those who turn to Him

knowing: Wudd is not a cold approval. It is warm, outward love, the kind that seeks closeness and shows itself. {idea}Al-Wadud loves His servants who turn to Him, and He is also the One they love most.{/idea} Scholars such as Ibn al-Qayyim explain that the name holds both meanings together: the Loving and the Beloved.

His love has its own path. The Quran does not say He loves the arrogant or the oppressive; it says He loves those who repent, who purify themselves, who do good, who are just and who trust Him. {idea}His love is open to everyone, and it is reached by turning towards Him.{/idea} Tell them, the Prophet ﷺ was told: if you love Allah, follow me, and Allah will love you and forgive you (3:31).

His love is unlike ours. We love out of need: we want company, comfort, something in return. Al-Wadud needs nothing. {reward}He loves you purely out of generosity, and then rewards you for loving Him.{/reward}
seeing: The name appears only twice in the Quran, both times beside forgiveness. Shu'ayb told his people, who had cheated in trade and mocked him, to seek forgiveness and return, for his Lord is Raheem and Wadud (11:90). The sinner who turns back is not merely tolerated; he is loved.

The second is in Surah Al-Buruj, right after the story of believers thrown into a burning trench for their faith: He is Al-Ghafur Al-Wadud (85:14). They saw only fire in this world. When they return to Him, they meet love. The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

His love also overflows into hearts. When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril and tells him to love that servant; Jibril calls out to the people of heaven, and then acceptance is placed for him on the earth (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). The Quran says Ar-Rahman will appoint affection for those who believe and do good (19:96). He told Musa, whose life had passed through the river, a palace and the desert: I cast upon you love from Me (20:39).
trusting: When you are tested, the question comes: if He loves me, why this? {trap}Reading every hardship as rejection forgets that the prophets, the most loved, were the most tested.{/trap} Musa's whole difficult path was framed by His love. Trust that the One who loves you is preparing you, not discarding you.

If you feel little love for Him, start where the Quran starts. Just before praising the believers who love Allah more than anything (2:165), it lists the heavens and earth, the ships, the rain and the winds as signs. {reward}Love grows from noticing what He has given you{/reward}, and from spending time with His words, which are the closest thing to His company in this life.
loving: When you love someone, you treasure everything that reminds you of them. The lover of Allah sees His traces everywhere: in the sky, in water, in the Quran, in the Prophet ﷺ. A man once asked the Prophet ﷺ when the Hour would come, and when asked what he had prepared, said only that he loved Allah and His Messenger. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ told him: you will be with those you love{/reward} (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).
now: You hear a friend say they love their mother, their partner, their team, and you realise you have never once said I love You to Allah, only asked Him for things. {idea}Al-Wadud is waiting for that sentence{/idea}. Say it tonight in sujud, in your own words, and mean it.
old: My relationship with Allah is mostly about rules, duty and fear of getting it wrong.
new: Al-Wadud loves those who turn to Him, and my obedience can grow out of love for Him.
try: Spend ten minutes today outside without your phone, noticing three things in creation, and thank Him for each one by name.

dua.text: Ya Wadud, I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of every deed that brings me closer to Your love.
dua.note: Call on Him as Al-Wadud when you feel unloved or far from Him; His love is reached by turning back, as Shu'ayb told his people (11:90).

pairs.why: Ghafur Wadud: He forgives the one who returns, and then loves him (85:14).
Raheem Wadud: mercy that reaches the sinner who returns, and love that welcomes him (11:90).

faq.a: Al-Wadud means the Most Loving. It comes from wudd, warm and outward affection. Scholars explain that it means both the One who loves His righteous and repentant servants and the One who is loved by them more than anything else.

faq.q: How many times is Al-Wadud mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: The name Al-Wadud appears twice in the Quran: in 11:90, where Shu'ayb calls his Lord Raheem and Wadud, and in 85:14, where Allah is called Al-Ghafur Al-Wadud. Both times it is joined to forgiveness or mercy.

faq.q: How can I earn the love of Al-Wadud?
faq.a: The Quran links His love to following the Prophet ﷺ (3:31), repentance and purity (2:222), doing good, justice and trust in Him. The Prophet ﷺ conveyed that a servant keeps drawing near through voluntary deeds until Allah loves him (Sahih al-Bukhari).
